c.v: Silicone elastomeric roof coating

runs.v: is a liquid-applied membrane that stretches and recovers to accommodate the daily thermal movement of a low-slope roof, sealing it under one monolithic surface. The chemistry — silicone, acrylic, or polyurethane — is matched to the roof's ponding, dirt-pickup, and movement conditions.

Comparing silicone elastomeric roof coating Newark NJ quotes on aging flat roofs means comparing chemistries. Elastomeric coatings expand and contract with temperature changes; silicone adds ponding-water resistance, acrylic adds lower cost and cleaner aging, and polyurethane adds toughness.

sections.heading: Silicone Elastomeric Roof Coating We Provide in Newark, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing applies silicone elastomeric roof coating across Essex County and matches the coating chemistry to the roof, because the RCMA recognizes 3 liquid-applied elastomeric coating chemistries: silicone (ASTM D6694), acrylic (ASTM D6083), and polyurethane (ASTM D6947).

runs.v: Each forms a seamless waterproof membrane to stop leaks at seams and flashings over the existing roof.

Elastomeric describes the high elongation of the cured film: a Simiron TEKTOP silicone reaches 279% elongation per ASTM D412 and an Acrymax AF-130FR acrylic reaches 220% per ASTM D2370, per Simiron and Acrymax product data. Silicone cures with atmospheric moisture, so it keeps curing on cool days when water-based acrylic stalls, per Henry and the RCMA.

sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Silicone Elastomeric Roof Coating

runs.v: Silicone-vs-Acrylic Chemistry Selection

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing selects the elastomeric chemistry from the roof condition.

runs.v: Silicone governs a ponding roof; acrylic governs a draining, dust-prone roof, because it re-washes cleaner: a Henry Tropi-Cool silicone drops from 0.88 to 0.73 reflectance over 3 years while a Mule-Hide A-300 acrylic drops from 0.87 to 0.75, per the CRRC, Henry, and Mule-Hide.
Surface Prep and Dry-Film-Thickness Application

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing cleans the membrane, repairs and reinforces the details, then applies the coating to the dry-film thickness that sets the warranty length.

runs.v: Surface preparation includes cleaning and drying the roof: power washing is critical for removing contaminants, and a primer is no substitute for thorough cleaning, per the RCMA, Gaco, and Henry. High-solids silicone goes on at about 1.5 gallons per 100 square feet, and the renewable warranty scales with dry-film thickness on a 10/15/20-year scale, per the RCMA, Gaco, Henry, and Mule-Hide.
Reflectance, Not Insulation, in the NJ Climate

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing frames the elastomeric coating as a reflectance upgrade, not an insulation upgrade.

runs.v: A new white silicone coating reflects about 85% of sunlight (CRRC 0.80–0.88) with 0.85–0.92 emittance, per the CRRC and Mule-Hide, so energy efficiency comes from a cooler roof surface, not insulation, and Newark's heating-dominated IRC Climate Zone 4–5 adds a winter heating penalty, per the DOE.

sections.heading: Ponding Water, Freeze-Thaw, and Application Weather in New Jersey

c.v: Ponding water is where the chemistries split: silicone coatings do not degrade under standing water, while traditional acrylics re-emulsify.

runs.v: Silicone is the usual choice for flat roofs with drainage issues and is particularly useful in New Jersey's freeze-thaw cycles, because the film stays flexible in the cold. Application still needs a dry window: no rain or high humidity that leaves dew on the roof, and air at least 5°F above the dew point so condensation cannot form under the coat.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of Using Silicone Roof Coating?

c.v: Silicone's downsides decide where acrylic or polyurethane is the better coating system.

runs.v: Silicone holds dirt, so reflectance drops faster than acrylic's; cured silicone is slippery when wet, so walkways get added granules for traction; only silicone bonds to cured silicone, which locks every future recoat into silicone; it tears more easily than polyurethane under heavy foot traffic; and it costs more than acrylic.

sections.heading: Recoat or Full Replacement? How Long a Silicone Coating System Lasts

c.v: A silicone coating can last 10 to 20 years when properly applied, and roof coatings can extend a roof's service life by 10 to 20 years before a full replacement is needed.

runs.v: Annual inspections are recommended to check for damage, and a maintained silicone restoration is recoated with silicone, indefinitely in practice, without a full tear-off, while the roof structure and insulation stay dry.

faqs.q: Should you choose a silicone or an acrylic elastomeric roof coating?

runs.v: Choose silicone when ponding or standing water is present and acrylic when dirt pickup and recoatability matter. Silicone is itself elastomeric, so asking whether silicone beats elastomeric really means silicone versus acrylic.

faqs.q: What makes a roof coating elastomeric?

runs.v: An elastomeric roof coating stretches and recovers to accommodate the daily thermal movement of the roof, with a cured film reaching high elongation.

faqs.q: Should you repair, recoat, or replace your roof?

runs.v: Recoat a low-slope roof when the membrane stays structurally sound without widespread saturation; replace it when saturation spreads or the membrane fails across more than 25–30% of the area.

faqs.q: Does an elastomeric roof coating add R-value or insulation?

runs.v: No. An elastomeric roof coating adds negligible R-value and does not insulate; the energy effect comes from reflectance and emittance.

faqs.q: How much does a silicone elastomeric roof coating cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Silicone typically runs about $5.00–$9.00 per sq ft, a fraction of tear-off and replacement cost, and avoids landfill. Newark Quality Roofing gives a free estimate in writing.

faqs.q: How long does a silicone elastomeric roof coating last before recoating?

runs.v: A silicone elastomeric coating renews on a cycle of roughly 15–20 years and an acrylic on roughly 10–15 years.

faqs.q: Does a white elastomeric cool roof coating lower energy costs in New Jersey?

runs.v: A white elastomeric coating reduces peak summer cooling demand by 11–27% in air-conditioned residential buildings, per the EPA, and a white silicone coating can cut roof surface temperature by more than 50°F, per the DOE. Liquid roof coatings can lower energy bills by 15% to 30%, less in a heating-dominated climate.

faqs.q: How much does 5 gallons of elastomeric roof coating cover on a flat roof?

runs.v: About 330 square feet of high-solids silicone at 1.5 gallons per 100 square feet, or roughly 200 to 250 square feet of two-coat acrylic, which needs more wet film for the same dry thickness.

faqs.q: How much does a coating save compared with a full roof replacement?

runs.v: Roof coatings typically save 50–70% compared with a full roof replacement, with no tear-off labor, no disposal fees, and no new insulation, and most projects finish in 1–3 days.

faqs.q: Is a silicone elastomeric coating ENERGY STAR rated?

runs.v: No roof coating carries a current ENERGY STAR label; the EPA ended its roof program in 2022, and the Cool Roof Rating Council now rates reflectance. Check utility rebates before counting on one.

faqs.q: Can an elastomeric coating go over modified bitumen, metal, or spray foam?

runs.v: Yes, once the substrate is clean, dry, and primed where its condition requires; the primer and the chemistry change with the roof type.
